children: Dillard's

on Friday said it would transfer its primary listings from the NYSE to the Texas Stock Exchange, joining a string of companies heading to the fledgling bourse that aims to challenge the two dominant US national stock exchanges.

Texas has long pitched itself as a lightly regulated, corporate-friendly alternative to the US coastal states, and TXSE's backers say the new exchange will mirror that environment, countering the trend of "more regulation, more taxation" in New York and other established financial hubs.
Besides the fashion retailer, regional lenders Origin Bancorp
and Texas Capital Bancshares
announced earlier this month that they would shift their listings to the TXSE from the New York Stock Exchange and the Nasdaq, respectively.
All three companies are slated to begin trading on the new exchange in October.

While the TXSE is pitching Texas' business-friendly laws and regulations to attract listings, companies on the new exchange must also be incorporated in Texas to benefit from the state's legal and regulatory protections.
Several major corporations have already relocated their headquarters to Texas, some citing a 2025 state law that bolsters corporate defenses against shareholder lawsuits, including Exxon Mobil
and Elon Musk's Tesla
and SpaceX
. None of these, however, have shifted their primary stock listings to the TXSE.
The new exchange is backed by Wall Street investors including BlackRock
, Citadel Securities and Charles Schwab
. Kelcy Warren, a Texas-based billionaire and executive chairman of pipeline operator Energy Transfer
, also had a significant stake in TXSE ​Group as of 2025, according to an SEC filing.
Earlier this month, the pipeline operator joined midstream energy services provider USA Compression Partners
and fuel distribution firms Sunoco LP
and SunocoCorp LLC
in announcing a shift in primary listings to the TXSE by early October. All four companies are headquartered in Texas.
